source_manifest.purpose: Composite candidate qualification; no causal attribution to an individual change

dataset.name: citation-entailment-challenge-v1
dataset.license: synthetic, CC0 — hand-written examples, no external corpus
dataset.description: Adversarial claim/evidence panel for the entailment assessor, deliberately harder than citation-entailment-v1. Every item is designed so a lexical-overlap assessor is misled: the passage shares the claim's vocabulary but a semantic reader must reject or invert the naive match. Categories: `numeric_conflict` (the passage reports the opposite direction or an incompatible magnitude with no explicit negation cue), `species_mismatch` (evidence is in a different organism/model than the claim asserts), `temporal_mismatch` (evidence is about a different time window or endpoint), `topic_mention_only` (the passage mentions every keyword but never asserts the claimed relationship), `retracted` (the only supporting passage is a retracted study and must not count as support), `paraphrase_support` (an entailing passage restates the claim with little shared vocabulary), and `paraphrase_contradiction` (a contradicting passage with no lexicon negation marker). Expected labels use supports/contradicts/insufficient. A retracted or unavailable source yields insufficient because no admissible passage supports the claim. Synthetic and legally shareable; NOT Google's private set. Human audit and threshold selection remain an external gap (no annotator panel).

items.claim: Drug A increases progression-free survival in glioblastoma.
passages: In the phase III cohort, Drug A shortened progression-free survival relative to placebo, from 9.2 months to 6.1 months.
items.label: contradicts

items.claim: Kinase X inhibition reduces AML tumor growth by roughly half.
passages: Kinase X inhibition increased AML tumor volume threefold across the cell lines tested.
items.label: contradicts

items.claim: Compound C lowers pathogen P viability at micromolar doses.
passages: Compound C raised pathogen P colony counts at every micromolar dose evaluated.
items.label: contradicts

items.claim: Blocking receptor Y restores CD8 T-cell infiltration.
passages: Blocking receptor Y further depleted CD8 T cells from the tumor microenvironment.
items.label: contradicts

items.claim: Vaccine V raises neutralizing antibody titers by ten-fold.
passages: Vaccine V produced neutralizing antibody titers indistinguishable from the unvaccinated arm.
items.label: contradicts

items.claim: Metabolic reprogramming via Z sensitizes human tumors to therapy.
passages: Metabolic reprogramming via Z sensitized murine xenograft tumors to therapy; human tissue was not examined.
items.label: insufficient

items.claim: Pathway W drives fibrosis progression in human lung.
passages: Pathway W drove fibrosis progression in a zebrafish fin-regeneration model.
items.label: insufficient

items.claim: Gene G confers drug resistance in human breast carcinoma.
passages: Gene G conferred drug resistance in Drosophila S2 cell culture assays.
items.label: insufficient

items.claim: Vaccine V elicits durable antibody responses at twelve months.
passages: Vaccine V elicited strong antibody responses when measured at day 14 post-immunization; later timepoints were not reported.
items.label: insufficient

items.claim: Drug A improves five-year overall survival in glioblastoma.
passages: Drug A improved the 30-day tumor response rate in glioblastoma; overall survival was not assessed.
items.label: insufficient

items.claim: Inhibiting kinase X reduces tumor growth in AML.
passages: Kinase X is a serine/threonine kinase frequently discussed in the context of AML tumor growth and cell proliferation.
items.label: insufficient

items.claim: Target T is druggable in solid tumors.
passages: Target T, its solid-tumor expression, and the general concept of druggability have attracted considerable research interest.
items.label: insufficient

items.claim: Compound C is effective against pathogen P.
passages: This review surveys many compounds, including compound C, and many pathogens, including pathogen P, without reporting new efficacy data.
items.label: insufficient

items.claim: Protein Q folds via a two-state mechanism.
passages: Protein Q folding has been studied for decades, and two-state versus multi-state mechanisms remain debated.
items.label: insufficient

items.claim: Drug A improves survival in glioblastoma.
passages: RETRACTED: Drug A improved survival in glioblastoma. This article has been retracted for image duplication and unreliable data.
items.label: insufficient

items.claim: Gene G is associated with disease D.
passages: This study reporting that gene G is associated with disease D was retracted after the cohort was found to be fabricated.
items.label: insufficient

items.claim: Kinase X inhibition reduces AML tumor growth.
passages: Pharmacologic blockade of the X kinase curtailed leukemic blast expansion in acute myeloid malignancies.
items.label: supports

items.claim: Blocking receptor Y restores immune surveillance.
passages: Antagonism of the Y receptor re-enabled the host's ability to detect and eliminate transformed cells.
items.label: supports

items.claim: Metabolic reprogramming via Z sensitizes cells to therapy.
passages: Rewiring cellular energetics through the Z axis lowered the treatment threshold at which cells succumbed.
items.label: supports

items.claim: Protein Q folds via a two-state mechanism.
passages: Q adopts its native structure through a single cooperative transition with no detectable intermediate.
items.label: supports

items.claim: Compound C is effective against pathogen P.
passages: Across all assays, pathogen P grew just as vigorously in the presence of compound C as in its absence.
items.label: contradicts

items.claim: Blocking receptor Y restores immune surveillance.
passages: Antagonizing the Y receptor left the animals just as unable to reject tumors as before treatment.
items.label: contradicts

items.claim: Metabolic reprogramming via Z sensitizes cells to therapy.
passages: Shifting cellular metabolism through the Z axis made the cells markedly more tolerant of the same therapy.
items.label: contradicts

items.claim: Compound C is effective against pathogen P.
passages: Treatment with compound C sharply curtailed the proliferation of the P organism in culture.
items.label: supports

items.claim: Pathway W drives fibrosis progression.
passages: Genetic ablation of pathway W accelerated fibrosis, whereas its activation was protective.
items.label: contradicts

items.claim: Drug A improves survival in glioblastoma.
passages: Glioblastoma remains lethal, and many agents such as drug A are under active investigation for survival benefit.
items.label: insufficient

items.claim: Vaccine V elicits durable antibody responses in humans.
passages: Vaccine V elicited durable antibody responses in rhesus macaques; a human trial has not been conducted.
items.label: insufficient

items.claim: Gene G is associated with disease D.
passages: Carriers of the G locus showed a markedly elevated incidence of the D phenotype in the cohort.
items.label: supports

items.claim: Target T inhibition slows solid tumor growth.
passages: Inhibiting target T accelerated solid tumor growth in every model examined.
items.label: contradicts

items.claim: Compound C durably suppresses pathogen P over four weeks.
passages: Compound C suppressed pathogen P at the 24-hour readout; suppression at later timepoints was not measured.
items.label: insufficient

report.external_gap: Human-audited representative sample and threshold calibration not performed (no annotator panel); synthetic dataset only. Retraction handling is upstream of this assessor (retracted sources are quarantined before grounding), so a retracted-passage item scored here isolates only the assessor, not the full pipeline.
